note_tweet.text:
35B parameters on a phone. Sounds like a lot to squeeze into RAM.

Here's the thing: not all the experts need to be in memory at the same time.

With Edge0-35B, we keep expert weights in local storage and bring in the ones needed for inference.

We also use a trained prerouter to predict which experts are needed next, so we can start loading them while the model is still working on the current token.

Still a 35B model. Just a smarter way to handle its memory.

Privacy by design.

Local inference lets prompts, files, and outputs stay on-device.

That means you can process sensitive documents or personal information without sending them to a third-party inference service

Lower latency when network delays matter.

Local inference removes the cloud round trip. That can improve responsiveness when network delay is a bottleneck.

Overall response time still depends on the model, hardware, and workload.

Works offline.

Once the model and runtime are installed, inference can keep running without internet.

Useful for an in-car assistant in a tunnel, a robot with unreliable Wi-Fi, or equipment at a remote site.

AI that works in airplane mode?

Welcome to on-device AI: the model runs on your phone or computer.

Inference can work offline, avoid cloud round trips, and keep your data on the device.

Here’s where those benefits matter. https://t.co/ZppMhhTfdB

data.text:
Edge0 brings open-source 8B and 35B AI models to consumer devices, with runtimes for macOS, iOS, Android and Windows.

Want to keep your AI workflow on-device?

Code and setup: https://t.co/6TrEfyTlry

Discord: https://t.co/wHJXOvr870

Local AI makes sense for:

- Private documents and notes
- Proprietary source code
- Sensitive internal workflows
- Offline applications

Of course, local doesn't mean risk-free. Device security, application permissions and backups still matter.

And local AI doesn't have to mean a high-end GPU workstation.

Edge0's optimized 35B model can run on a 16 GB M2 Mac.

We've even run it on an iPhone 16 Pro.

Your own laptop or phone can handle inference without sending prompts to a cloud model.

When you use a hosted AI model, your prompts travel to the provider's infrastructure for processing.

Even with strong security measures, that's another place where your data has to be handled and protected.

Local inference removes that transfer.

Your data doesn't have to leave your device for AI to work.

With local AI, your prompts, files, and model outputs can stay on your own device.

No need to send every request to someone else's servers.

And you don't need expensive hardware to do it. https://t.co/m70aPFdVtW
